There’s definitely a chance these efforts could reduce future harm, but only if governments scale up commitments, enforce stronger regulations, curb fossil fuel lobbying, and support a just transition for workers and vulnerable communities.

I’m most excited about a mix of big-picture policy and on-the-ground action. Things I think could actually move the needle: strong national policies that phase out fossil fuels (end subsidies, put a price on carbon), massive investment in renewables and grid upgrades, electrifying transport, and funding climate resilience for vulnerable communities (better coastal defenses, drought-resistant crops, water infrastructure). Nature-based solutions — reforestation, wetland restoration — also help with carbon and local flood protection.
